summary: Iteration 18 (backend only): verified the courtroom/trial system added on top of the law-jail overhaul. Ran existing 18 courtroom unit tests + 13 law_jail_overhaul + 11 t1_guard + 9 law_refactor unit tests (50 total). Added 10 new live-API integration tests in test_courtroom_live_api.py covering surrender guards, dismissal-on-clean-record, trial GET shape, /defend & /rest-case 'no active trial' 400 guards, auth requirement, and source-level checks that BOTH surrender and _auto_arrest_and_imprison delegate to the shared create_trial_from_open_crimes helper. 60/60 tests pass (100%).

critical_code_review_comments: routes/law.py:character_surrender correctly delegates to create_trial_from_open_crimes (line 107) — no direct imprisonment on surrender. Guards in correct order: imprisoned check → already-on-trial check → no-crimes dismissal → trial creation.

server.py:_auto_arrest_and_imprison (lines 1468-1544) correctly routes through create_trial_from_open_crimes (line 1519). Also seeds a 'resisting_authority' minor crime when AI flags arrest with no open crimes, so the trial has charges to consider — matches choice (3a) trigger on both manual surrender AND auto-arrest.
server.py:/api/locations/{nation}/{location}/roleplay (lines 1620-1642) correctly enforces 403 (wrong location) and 409 (at courthouse) when a trial is in_session.

create_trial_from_open_crimes (routes/courtroom.py:33) is well-structured: looks up bounty, resolves city, ensures courthouse + judge + prosecutor NPCs, gathers witnesses, starts trial, publishes Chronicle event. All idempotent operations.
CourtroomService.append_defence_turn clamps leniency in [-100, +100] — verified by test_leniency_clamps_at_100 and test_leniency_clamps_at_minus_100.
_execute_verdict handles all 5 sentence types (imprison/fine/exile/execute/dismissed); execute path even generates an eulogy via memorial._generate_eulogy and marks character is_active=False.
Per-turn AI call uses gpt-4o and verdict uses gpt-4o-mini — costs are kept low. AI failures are wrapped in try/except → 502 with detail, so the trial state is not corrupted on transient AI errors.
No file-size issue: courtroom_service.py and routes/courtroom.py are each well under 700 lines.
MongoDB _id is properly excluded (every find_one uses {'_id': 0, ...} projection).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Live API tests for courtroom system live at /app/backend/tests/test_courtroom_live_api.py. To run, export both MONGO_URL (from /app/backend/.env) and REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL (from /app/frontend/.env) before invoking pytest. The happy-path defend → verdict flow consumes LLM credits (gpt-4o + gpt-4o-mini per turn) so live tests should avoid actually starting a trial that needs to be advanced through the AI. Use the dismissal path or seed a trial directly in the FakeDB for unit-level coverage. The auto-arrest path is gated by the AI returning arrest_executed:true in analyze_interaction — hard to drive in a deterministic test; code review on _auto_arrest_and_imprison (server.py:1468-1544) is the recommended verification.
rca of the issue: No issues found. The trial system has been correctly extended from the law-jail overhaul: surrender + auto-arrest both delegate to the shared create_trial_from_open_crimes helper, RP is correctly locked out during active trials, leniency is properly clamped, and all 5 verdict types route to the correct resolution. The system is production-ready.
